            f.unlink()


def build(run_id: str, runs_dir="runs", out="site/data", counties=None, data_root=None) -> list[str]:
    if run_id == "latest":
        run_id = latest_run(runs_dir)
    run_dir = Path(runs_dir) / run_id
    out = Path(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    meta = json.loads((run_dir / "run.json").read_text()) if (run_dir / "run.json").exists() else {}
    if meta.get("resumed_from"):
        tot = total_seconds(meta, runs_dir)
        if tot is not None:
            meta["seconds_total"] = tot
    summary = json.loads((run_dir / "summary.json").read_text()) if (run_dir / "summary.json").exists() else None
    by_summary = {c["county"]: c for c in (summary or {}).get("counties", [])}
    # the run's own order when it kept one; else the folders' (alphabetical)
    keys = [c["county"] for c in (summary or {}).get("counties", [])] or sorted(p.parent.name for p in run_dir.glob("*/county.json"))
    if counties:
        keys = [k for k in keys if k in counties]
    if not keys:
        raise SystemExit(f"no county.json under {run_dir}")
    index = {"run": run_id, "started": meta.get("started"), "ended": meta.get("ended"), "counties": [], "summary": {},
             "run_totals": {k: meta[k] for k in ("model_calls", "prompt_tokens", "completion_tokens",
                                                 "metered_cost_estimate") if k in meta}}
    for key in keys:
        raw = json.loads((run_dir / key / "county.json").read_text())
        summ = by_summary.get(key)
        if (summ or {}).get("status") == "unchecked" or raw.get("layout") == "no_printed_totals":
            index["counties"].append(unchecked_entry(key, summ, raw))
            continue
        _clear(out, key)
        fpath = run_dir / key / "findings.json"
        findings = json.loads(fpath.read_text()) if fpath.exists() else None
        report = raw.get("layout") == "report"
        rows, images = None, None
        if report:
            # the page images of a report county are written only for the pages that carry a finding, and page 1
            images = {1} | {f["page"] for f in (findings or {}).get("findings", []) if f.get("page")}
            images &= {p["number"] for p in raw["pages"]}
            sizes = frame_sizes(raw)
            sizes.update(render_pages(key, sorted(images), out / "pages", data_root))
            crops, tots = wanted_rows(raw, findings)
            from PIL import Image
            from .render import page_png
            from .sources import DATA
            frame = {p["number"]: p.get("width") or sizes[p["number"]][0] for p in raw["pages"]}

            def im_of(n, _k=key):
                with Image.open(page_png(_k, n, CROP_DPI, data_root or DATA)) as im:
                    return im.convert("L")
            rc, fx, rcix = build_rows(raw, crops, tots, im_of, frame.get, lambda n: sizes[n][2] / frame[n], out / "rows",
                                      lambda county, n: f"data/rows/{county}-r{n}.webp")
            rows = {"rc": rc, "fx": fx, "rcix": rcix}
            inks, rules = {}, {}
        else:
            sizes = render_pages(key, [p["number"] for p in raw["pages"]], out / "pages", data_root)
            inks, rules = render_blocks(raw, sizes, out / "blocks", data_root)
        crops_dir = out / "crops"

        def crop_path(county, gid, src, _dir=run_dir / key):
            if not src or not (_dir / src).exists():
                return None
            crops_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copyfile(_dir / src, crops_dir / f"{county}-{gid}.png")
            return f"data/crops/{county}-{gid}.png"

        run = dict(meta)
        for src, dst in (("seconds", "seconds"), ("metered_cost", "metered_cost_estimate"), ("model_calls_by_model", "model_calls_by_model"),
                         ("reader", "reader")):
            if (summ or {}).get(src) is not None:      # a run of every county: the county's own figures, not the run's
                run[dst] = summ[src]
        if raw.get("sample") and not run.get("sample"):
            run["sample"] = raw["sample"]
        d = build_county(raw, sizes, ink=inks, rules=rules, findings=findings, run=run,
                         findings_path=fpath.as_posix() if findings else None,
                         evidence=f"data/{key}-findings.json" if findings else None, crop_path=crop_path,
                         rows=rows, images=images)
        if findings:
            shutil.copyfile(fpath, out / f"{key}-findings.json")
        (out / f"{key}.json").write_text(json.dumps(d, separators=(",", ":")))
        index["counties"].append(county_entry(key, summ, findings, len(d["pages"]), raw.get("layout") or ""))
        index["summary"][key] = raw.get("summary", {})
    if counties and (out / "index.json").exists():
        # a build of some counties keeps the entries of the others that an earlier build of this run wrote
        old = json.loads((out / "index.json").read_text())
        if old.get("run") == run_id:
            built = {c["key"] for c in index["counties"]}
            mine = {c["key"]: c for c in index["counties"]}
            mine.update({c["key"]: c for c in old["counties"] if c["key"] not in built})
            order = [c["county"] for c in (summary or {}).get("counties", [])] or sorted(mine)
            index["counties"] = [mine[k] for k in order if k in mine]
            index["summary"] = {**old.get("summary", {}), **index["summary"]}
    index["totals"] = run_totals(index["counties"], summary, meta)
    (out / "index.json").write_text(json.dumps(index, separators=(",", ":")))
    return keys


def frame_sizes(raw: dict, max_width=MAX_WIDTH) -> dict:
    """The sizes of the pages without rendering them: (frame_w, frame_h, img_w, img_h) from the sizes the run recorded."""
    out = {}
    for pg in raw["pages"]:
        w, h = pg.get("width"), pg.get("height")
        if not w or not h:
            raise ValueError(f"page {pg['number']} of {raw['county']} has no recorded size")
        iw = min(max_width, w)
        out[pg["number"]] = (w, h, iw, round(h * iw / w))
    return out

"""Shared bits for the T07c scripts: a static server over site/, and a page opener that collects errors."""
import http.server, socketserver, threading, functools, pathlib
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
OUT = ROOT / "qa" / "t07c"
class Quiet(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *a, **k): pass
srv = socketserver.TCPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), functools.partial(Quiet, directory=str(ROOT / "site")))
threading.Thread(target=srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
BASE = f"http://127.0.0.1:{srv.server_address[1]}/"

def open_page(b, w, h, q="", wait=2600, **kw):
    ctx = b.new_context(viewport={"width": w, "height": h}, **kw); pg = ctx.new_page()
    errs = []
    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append(str(e)))
    pg.on("console", lambda m: errs.append(m.text) if m.type == "error" else None)
    pg.goto(BASE + q, wait_until="load"); pg.wait_for_timeout(wait)
    return ctx, pg, errs
"""axe-core (qa/axe.min.js, injected) at 1440x900 and 390x844 on each state T07c adds. Writes qa/t07c/axe.json.
python3 qa/t07c/axe.py"""
import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, str(__import__("pathlib").Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from lib import *
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
AXE = (ROOT / "qa" / "axe.min.js").read_text()
TAGS = ["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa", "wcag22aa"]

def tab_focus(pg):
    pg.locator("#tabs [aria-selected=true]").focus(); pg.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); pg.wait_for_timeout(200)

def replay_paused(pg):
    pg.get_by_role("button", name="Replay the audit").click()
    pg.wait_for_function("document.getElementById('rp-cap').textContent.startsWith('Page 2: the printed sum')", timeout=60000)
    pg.wait_for_timeout(1200); pg.keyboard.press("Escape"); pg.wait_for_timeout(300)

CASES = [("Panola (opening)", "", None), ("San Saba (opening)", "?county=san_saba", None),
         ("San Saba (a row nothing can decide)", "?county=san_saba&finding=f003", None), ("Jones (a settled row)", "?county=jones&finding=f009", None),
         ("Jones (a column sum in the finding)", "?county=jones&finding=f001", None), ("Lynn (wrong column)", "?county=lynn&finding=f004", None),
         ("Scurry (rows only the file has)", "?county=scurry", None), ("Cottle (nothing found)", "?county=cottle", None),
         ("Limestone (not checked)", "?county=limestone", None), ("tabs with keyboard focus", "?county=jones", tab_focus),
         ("San Saba replay paused (a row read again)", "?county=san_saba", replay_paused)]
res, total = [], 0
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch()
    for w, h in [(1440, 900), (390, 844)]:
        for name, q, act in CASES:
            ctx, pg, errs = open_page(b, w, h, q, wait=2800)
            if act: act(pg)
            pg.evaluate(AXE)
            r = pg.evaluate("tags => axe.run(document, {runOnly: {type: 'tag', values: tags}})", TAGS)
            v = [{"id": x["id"], "impact": x["impact"], "help": x["help"], "nodes": [{"target": n["target"], "summary": n.get("failureSummary", "")[:300]} for n in x["nodes"]]} for x in r["violations"]]
            total += len(v)
            res.append({"case": name, "viewport": f"{w}x{h}", "violations": v, "passes": len(r["passes"]), "incomplete": [x["id"] for x in r["incomplete"]], "pageErrors": errs})
            print(w, name, len(v), [x["id"] for x in v], flush=True)
            ctx.close()
    b.close()
(OUT / "axe.json").write_text(json.dumps({"axe": "4.12.1", "tags": TAGS, "violations_total": total, "runs": res}, indent=1))
print("total violations", total)
"""Behaviour checks for T07c, results in qa/t07c/checks.json:  python3 qa/t07c/check.py
tabs (one tab stop, arrow keys, ?county=, sideways scroll inside the bar on a small screen), the run line, the states, a whole
replay of San Saba and of Cottle, the loupe's figure size, and the page's width at four window sizes."""
import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, str(__import__("pathlib").Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from lib import *
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

R = {}
def note(k, v): R[k] = v; print(k, json.dumps(v)[:300], flush=True)

with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch()
    # tabs
    ctx, pg, errs = open_page(b, 1440, 900, "?county=lynn", wait=2500)
    tabs = pg.evaluate("[...document.querySelectorAll('#tabs button')].map(b => ({text: b.textContent.replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim(), stop: b.tabIndex === 0, sel: b.getAttribute('aria-selected')}))")
    note("tabs", tabs)
    note("tab_stops", sum(t["stop"] for t in tabs))
    note("selected_by_query", [t["text"] for t in tabs if t["sel"] == "true"])
    pg.locator("#tabs [aria-selected=true]").focus()
    pg.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); a = pg.evaluate("document.activeElement.textContent.replace(/\\s+/g,' ').trim()")
    pg.keyboard.press("End"); e = pg.evaluate("document.activeElement.textContent.replace(/\\s+/g,' ').trim()")
    pg.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); w = pg.evaluate("document.activeElement.textContent.replace(/\\s+/g,' ').trim()")
    pg.keyboard.press("Home"); h = pg.evaluate("document.activeElement.textContent.replace(/\\s+/g,' ').trim()")
    note("arrow_keys", {"ArrowRight": a, "End": e, "ArrowRight_wraps": w, "Home": h})
    pg.keyboard.press("Enter"); pg.wait_for_timeout(2500)
    note("enter_opens", {"url": pg.evaluate("location.search"), "selected": pg.evaluate("document.querySelector('#tabs [aria-selected=true]').textContent.replace(/\\s+/g,' ').trim()"),
                         "card": pg.evaluate("document.querySelector('#card h2') ? document.querySelector('#card h2').textContent : null")})
    note("run_line", pg.evaluate("document.getElementById('runline').textContent"))
    note("errors_tabs", errs); ctx.close()
    # small screen: the tabs scroll inside the bar, the page does not move
    ctx, pg, errs = open_page(b, 390, 844, "?county=foard", wait=2500)
    note("tabs_390", pg.evaluate("(() => { const n = document.getElementById('tabs'); return {scrolls_inside: n.scrollWidth > n.clientWidth, bar_h: document.querySelector('.bar').offsetHeight, page_overflow: document.documentElement.scrollWidth > innerWidth, tab_h: document.querySelector('#tabs button').offsetHeight}; })()"))
    note("run_line_above_stage_390", pg.evaluate("(() => { const r = document.getElementById('runline').getBoundingClientRect(), s = document.getElementById('stage').getBoundingClientRect(); return {runline_bottom: Math.round(r.bottom), stage_top: Math.round(s.top)}; })()"))
    ctx.close()
    # no sideways scroll
    for w, h in ((1440, 900), (1024, 768), (390, 844), (320, 640)):
        for q in ("", "?county=jones&finding=f009", "?county=cottle", "?county=limestone"):
            ctx, pg, errs = open_page(b, w, h, q, wait=1800)
            note(f"overflow_{w}_{q or 'panola'}", pg.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollWidth > innerWidth || document.body.scrollWidth > innerWidth"))

# One prompt to a general coding agent, scored against the audit (Panola County)

Figures come from `docs/evidence/baseline/score.json` (written by
`uv run crossfoot score --findings docs/evidence/baseline/findings.json --county panola --resume latest`),
`docs/evidence/baseline/run.json`, and the audit's run files `runs/20261011-135350/` and `runs/20261011-130414/`.
Every statement the baseline made about the scan is that agent's own reading, quoted as such; nobody has checked it by eye, and
nothing here is a statement about a county's certified results. These are differences between a volunteer dataset and the
printed scan. The county's scan and the volunteer file are public sources and neither has seen or approved this.

## What the baseline was given and how it was run

From `baseline/run.json`: one prompt (`baseline/prompt.txt`) to Claude Code, headless (`claude -p`), model `claude-sonnet-5-5`, in an
empty folder holding only the Panola scan (`scan.pdf`) and the published file (`published.csv`). Tools allowed: Bash, Read, Write, Edit,
Glob, Grep, TodoWrite; web tools and curl/wget disallowed. Started 2026-10-11T09:28:04Z. 79 turns (30 Bash, 25 Read calls),
411 seconds, cost 1.5254 US dollars "api equivalent" (the run file's own label; not a gateway-metered figure). No follow-up prompt.
It listed 74 findings (`findings.json`) and wrote a summary (`summary.md`).

## How it was scored

`crossfoot score` matches each claimed disagreement (office, candidate, precinct, part, file value, scan value) to the audit's
newest Panola findings (run `20261011-135350`) with the audit's own label matching (`audit.nk`, `audit.candidate_key`), then puts it in
one group. Nothing in the audit was changed to suit the list; the only change to `audit.py` in this task adds the printed total used on
each side to the sum records. No model was called.

## The two sides

| | One prompt (baseline) | Crossfoot audit |
|---|---|---|
| Findings listed | 74 | 121 (46 groups) |
| Settled by printed totals | 73 | 109 |
# Recovery evidence

## A run stopped by its budget and continued

Two small counties (San Saba, Cottle), real model calls, run 20261011-135519 (`runs/20261011-135519/`; trace of the resumed part, Cottle: `6b289ce0c777683ca054674468c29dbd`; none found for the first part). Ledger events and
the counts come from `runs/20261011-135519/ledger.sqlite` and `summary.json`. Evidence ids are in `.prod-build/evidence.jsonl`.

1. `crossfoot audit --all --only san_saba,cottle --budget 0.25` (E0071, exit 2, expected)
   - Last lines of the run's summary: San Saba `audited` (33 calls, $0.2076); Cottle `stopped`: "run budget $0.25 reached
     (estimated spend $0.2573 after 39 calls); refusing the next call". "1 of 2 counties closed."
   - Ledger after the stop: San Saba 1,100 cells, 1,100 accepted, 21 page reads, `read_done` written. Cottle 168 cells read from 3
     pages, 0 accepted, no `read_done`.
2. `crossfoot audit --all --only san_saba,cottle --resume 20261011-135519 --budget 2` (E0072, exit 0)
   - Last lines: "san_saba skipped: closed in the run being continued"; "cottle end: audited; 21 calls, $0.1944, 95.5 s";
     "2 of 2 counties closed; model calls 61; metered cost (estimate) $0.4626".
   - Ledger after: San Saba still 1,100 cells, 1,100 accepted, 8 re-read tries, 21 page reads (unchanged: no page of it was
     read again). Cottle 664 cells, all accepted, 12 pages.

Counts: model calls San Saba 33 (first run only; the resume added none), Cottle 7 in the first run plus 21 in the resume = 28,
all 61 in the run. So nothing accepted was read again. What was paid twice: Cottle's three half-read pages (7 calls, about $0.06)
# Traces (neatlogs)

Written 11 October 2026 (task T05b; it replaces the T05 note that said the neatlogs server did not answer). The server answered.
Everything below was read from the neatlogs MCP server with `search_traces` and `get_trace_context`, and from `runs/*/run.json` (start times).
Dollar costs are not given: neatlogs reports cost 0 for every trace here.

## How to open one

1. `search_traces` with a word that appears in span text (`read_group`, `read_page`, `reread`, `choose_reader`, `san_saba`, `crossfoot`; limit up to 100).
   Each result has `trace_id`, `start_ts`, `root_span_name`, `span_count`, `total_tokens`.
2. `get_trace_context` with the full 32-character `trace_id` and `limit` 5 (the options `span_types`, `span_names`, `fields`, `max_chars_per_field`
   answer `not_enabled`). Add `include_evaluations: false` to keep the answer short.
3. No run file stores its trace id. A run is paired to a trace by its start time (`run.json` `started`, UTC) against the trace's `start_ts`
   (within a few seconds) and the root span name. 27 distinct traces came back from the searches; those are all that were looked at.

# Traces (neatlogs)

Written 11 October 2026 (task T05b; it replaces the T05 note that said the neatlogs server did not answer). The server answered.
Everything below was read from the neatlogs MCP server with `search_traces` and `get_trace_context`, and from `runs/*/run.json` (start times).
Dollar costs are not given: neatlogs reports cost 0 for every trace here.

## How to open one

1. `search_traces` with a word that appears in span text (`read_group`, `read_page`, `reread`, `choose_reader`, `san_saba`, `crossfoot`; limit up to 100).
   Each result has `trace_id`, `start_ts`, `root_span_name`, `span_count`, `total_tokens`.
2. `get_trace_context` with the full 32-character `trace_id` and `limit` 5 (the options `span_types`, `span_names`, `fields`, `max_chars_per_field`
   answer `not_enabled`). Add `include_evaluations: false` to keep the answer short.
3. No run file stores its trace id. A run is paired to a trace by its start time (`run.json` `started`, UTC) against the trace's `start_ts`
   (within a few seconds) and the root span name. 27 distinct traces came back from the searches; those are all that were looked at.

# Crossfoot — neatHack build log

## Project
**Crossfoot** audits published data against the scanned documents it was copied from, proves each error with the
document's own printed totals, and proposes the fix.

The problem it addresses: open datasets transcribed from scanned official documents carry silent errors that survive
manual checking. The first target is the eight Texas county files the OpenElections project uses as a manually
verified answer key for grading document-reading models.

## Team
Team Saharsh.

## Stack
Planned, and updated as each part is actually used:
- Python 3.12 with uv; SQLite for the run ledger; Pillow and pdftoppm for page images.
- Models through the event's LiteLLM gateway (`claude-haiku` first, `claude-sonnet-4.6` only for cells that fail).
- neatlogs for traces of every model and tool call.
- Entire for a checkpoint of the coding session behind every commit.
- cfo.ai for the business plan, built from the measured cost per county.
- A static results page (plain HTML, CSS and JS).

## Build log

### 2026-10-11 (hour 26 of the window)
- Planning came first: the idea, the contract (`.prod-build/contract.md`), the architecture (`ARCHITECTURE.md`), the
  UI specification (`UI-SPEC.md`) and the task plan (`.prod-build/plan.json`) were written before any code.
- Checked before writing code, with plain arithmetic on the public files and no model: two rows in the published
  answer files fail their own totals (one in Panola County, one in San Saba County). Reproduced by
  `crossfoot filecheck --all` once task T01 lands.
- How the code is written: each task is a separate coding session started in this folder, so the checkpoint tool
  records the session behind each commit.

### 2026-10-11 - T01 scaffold, sources, rendering, ledger, checks
- Added the uv project, `fetch`, `filecheck` and `render` commands, the SQLite ledger and the pure checks
  (`row_checks`, `column_checks`, `grid_gaps`, `locate`). No model was called.
- Measured with `uv run crossfoot filecheck --all` on the downloaded files: rows whose votes differ from the sum of
  their parts: Panola 1 of 764 checked, San Saba 1 of 275, the other six 0. Rows skipped for a blank part: Cottle 0,
  Foard 4, Jones 4, Limestone 875 (all rows; checked 0), Lynn 8, Panola 19, San Saba 0, Scurry 11.
- `uv run crossfoot render --county panola --page 1` wrote a 2781x1687 px PNG at 200 dpi.

"""Write the README's tables from the final run's files, so no figure in them is typed by hand.

    python3 tools/readme_tables.py            rewrite the blocks between <!-- name:start --> and <!-- name:end --> in README.md
    python3 tools/readme_tables.py --check    exit 1 if README.md differs from what the files give

Reads runs/<run>/summary.json (the newest run with one, or --run) and, for the picture, the findings.json and crop of the
run that the summary names for Panola."""
import argparse, json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FULL_RUN = "20261011-120008"          # the one full run of Panola from nothing, named in the README
PICTURE = ("panola", "f005")          # a settled finding whose crop shows the cell and the row sum


def latest_summary() -> str:
    ids = sorted(p.parent.name for p in (ROOT / "runs").glob("*/summary.json"))
    return ids[-1]


def n(v) -> str:
    return f"{v:,}"


def findings_table(s: dict) -> str:
    head = ("| County | Layout | Published rows compared | Disagreements | Settled by the printed totals | Cannot be verified "
            "| Printed sums in all | Holding with the published file | Holding with the corrected file |\n"
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    rows = []
    for c in s["counties"]:
        name = c["county"].replace("_", " ").title()
        if c["status"] != "audited":
            rows.append(f"| {name} | {c['layout']} | not checked: nothing printed on the scan can be summed | | | | | | |")
            continue
        sc, st = c["sums_check"], c["findings_by_status"]
        rows.append(f"| {name} | {c['layout']} | {n(c['rows_compared'])} of {n(c['rows_published'])} | {n(sum(st.values()))} "
                    f"| {n(st.get('settled_against_file', 0))} | {n(st.get('cannot_verify', 0))} | {n(sc['in_all'])} "
                    f"| {n(sc['holding_with_published'])} | {n(sc['holding_with_corrected'])} |")
    t = s["totals"]
    st, sc = t["findings_by_status"], t["sums_check"]
    rows.append(f"| **All** | | {n(t['rows_compared'])} of {n(t['rows_published'])} | {n(sum(st.values()))} "
                f"| {n(st.get('settled_against_file', 0))} | {n(st.get('cannot_verify', 0))} | {n(sc['in_all'])} "
                f"| {n(sc['holding_with_published'])} | {n(sc['holding_with_corrected'])} |")
    return "\n".join([head, *rows])


def cost_table(s: dict) -> str:
    head = "| County | Pages | Model calls | Metered cost (estimate) | Seconds |\n|---|---|---|---|---|"
    rows = [f"| {c['county'].replace('_', ' ').title()} | {c['pages']} | {c['model_calls']} | ${c['metered_cost']:.4f} | {c['seconds']} |"
            for c in s["counties"]]
    t = s["totals"]
    rows.append(f"| **All** | {sum(c['pages'] for c in s['counties'])} | {t['model_calls']} | ${t['metered_cost']:.4f} | {t['seconds']} |")
    full = json.loads((ROOT / "runs" / FULL_RUN / "run.json").read_text())
    note = (f"These are the figures of the audit that `summary.json` lists for each county; a county audited again from an "
            f"earlier run's ledger counts the new calls only, not the reading that was paid for in that earlier run. The one "
            f"full run of Panola from nothing, [`runs/{FULL_RUN}/run.json`](runs/{FULL_RUN}/run.json), took "
            f"{full['seconds']} seconds, {full['model_calls']} model calls and ${full['metered_cost_estimate']:.2f} (metered estimate).")
    return "\n".join([head, *rows, "", note])


def picture(s: dict) -> str:
    county, fid = PICTURE
    run = next(c["from_run"] for c in s["counties"] if c["county"] == county)
    base = f"runs/{run}/{county}"
    doc = json.loads((ROOT / base / "findings.json").read_text())
    f = next(x for x in doc["findings"] if x["id"] == fid)
    row = next(x for x in f["sums"] if x["kind"] == "row")
    part = f["part"].replace("_", " ")
    return (f"![crop of the scan: {f['candidate']}, precinct {f['precinct']}, the cell outlined]({base}/{f['crop']})\n\n"
            f"*Panola County, page {f['page']}, {f['candidate']}, precinct {f['precinct']}, {part}. The published file has "
            f"{f['file_value']}; the scan has {f['scan_value']}. The row's printed total is {row['printed']}: the cells add to "
            f"{row['computed_with_scan']} with the scan's value and to {row['computed_with_file']} with the file's, so the printed "
            f"total decides (finding {fid} in [{base}/findings.json]({base}/findings.json); not confirmed by a person).*")


def blocks(run: str) -> dict:
    s = json.loads((ROOT / "runs" / run / "summary.json").read_text())
    return {"table": findings_table(s), "cost": cost_table(s), "picture": picture(s), "run": f"`runs/{run}`"}


def apply(text: str, b: dict) -> str:
    for name, body in b.items():
        text = re.sub(rf"(<!-- {name}:start -->\n).*?(\n<!-- {name}:end -->)", lambda m: m.group(1) + body + m.group(2), text, flags=re.S)
    return text


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--run", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    run = a.run or latest_summary()
    path = ROOT / "README.md"
    old = path.read_text()
    new = apply(old, blocks(run))
    if a.check:
        print("README figures match the files" if new == old else "README figures differ from the files")
        return 0 if new == old else 1
    path.write_text(new)
    print(f"README.md blocks written from runs/{run}/summary.json")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

The audit's two runs are `20261011-130414` (the all-counties run; its Panola share is 168 calls, 0.7675 USD, 474.9 s) and

not as a like-for-like price.

The 36 findings the baseline's list lacks, from `score.json` `missed_settled`: 26 `wrong_precinct`, 5 `missing_row`, 2 `extra_row`,
2 `wrong_number`, 1 `file_row_fails_own_total`. By office: 25 in Constable, 8 in County Commissioner, 2 in U.S. Senate, 1 in a

## What each side hands a maintainer

cat > README.md <<'E'
# Crossfoot

Crossfoot is an agent that audits published data against the scanned documents it was copied from, proves each
error with the document's own printed totals, and proposes the fix.

<!-- picture:start -->
<!-- picture:end -->

## What it found

Eight Texas county files for the 2024 general election, each checked against its county's own scan. Every figure
below is made from [`runs/20261011-141300/summary.json`](runs/20261011-141300/summary.json) by
[`tools/readme_tables.py`](tools/readme_tables.py); each county's own folder holds its report, corrected file and crops.

<!-- table:start -->
<!-- table:end -->

Confirmed by a person: 0. Nothing has been sent to the project.

What these are: transcription slips in a volunteer dataset, found by comparing it with the counties' certified scans,
which are the source of truth. The scans and the published files are public
([scans](https://github.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/tree/master/2024/general),
[published files](https://github.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/tree/master/2024/counties), from the
[OpenElections](https://github.com/openelections) project). Neither the project nor any county has seen or approved
this. Nothing here says anything about the results themselves.

How to check one: open the county's `report.md` (for example
[Panola's](runs/20261011-135350/panola/report.md)). Each group has a crop of the scan, the cells, and each printed sum
with the value that makes it hold. Add the numbers on the crop yourself.

## How it works

1. Read a sample of the first page with a cheap model and choose the reader by how many printed row sums fail.
2. Read every page into a ledger, one cell at a time.
3. Check every printed sum: a value is accepted only when the sums it sits on hold.
4. Where two failing sums cross, look again at that cell with a bigger crop and, if needed, a stronger model.
5. Lay the published file over the closed ledger, row by row.
6. The printed sums decide: a correction is proposed only when a printed total agrees with the new value and
   disagrees with the old one; otherwise it says "cannot verify" and leaves the value alone.

## Run it

```
uv sync
export LITELLM_API_KEY=... LITELLM_BASE_URL=...      # an OpenAI-compatible gateway; NEATLOGS_API_KEY is optional
uv run crossfoot budget                              # the gateway's spend and limit for the key
uv run crossfoot audit --county panola               # read, close, audit one county; writes runs/<run_id>/panola/
uv run crossfoot audit --all --budget 9              # every county in turn; writes runs/<run_id>/<county>/ and summary.json, summary.md
uv run crossfoot summarize --base <run_id> --use panola=<run_id>   # a new summary from the newest result of each county; no model call
uv run crossfoot verify-known --county panola        # checks the findings against eight slips read by eye
uv run crossfoot site build --run latest             # writes site/data/ from the newest summary run
python3 -m http.server -d site 8000                  # then open http://localhost:8000/
uv run pytest -q                                     # no network, no model calls
```

It needs `pdftoppm` (poppler) to render the scans. `uv run crossfoot --help` lists the other steps.

## Evidence

- Two changes made from what the runs showed, each with a run before and a run after and what got worse:
  [docs/evidence/before-after.md](docs/evidence/before-after.md).
- One prompt to a general coding agent on the same county, scored the same way:
  [docs/evidence/baseline.md](docs/evidence/baseline.md).
- A run stopped by its budget and continued, and other recoveries:
  [docs/evidence/recovery.md](docs/evidence/recovery.md).
- Traces and the detection: [docs/evidence/traces.md](docs/evidence/traces.md).
- Checkpoints, the output of `entire checkpoint list`: [docs/evidence/checkpoints.txt](docs/evidence/checkpoints.txt)
  (the last line says how to open a session from a commit's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer).
- The results page: [site/](site/) (static; serve it as in "Run it"). Screenshots of it at 1440x900 and 390x844 and the
  accessibility check (axe-core, zero violations) are in [qa/final/](qa/final/).
- The build log, including what failed: [hackathon.md](hackathon.md).

Measured cost and time per county, from the same summary:

<!-- cost:start -->
<!-- cost:end -->

## The three tools

- **neatlogs.** Every model and tool call is a span. Two changes to the program were made from what the runs showed
  ([before-after.md](docs/evidence/before-after.md)), and one detection was created
  ([traces.md](docs/evidence/traces.md)).
- **Entire.** Every coding session's commit carries an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer
  ([checkpoints.txt](docs/evidence/checkpoints.txt)). The graph plugin's instructions for coding agents are in
  [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## Limits

- The sums cannot see two wrong values that cancel out on the same row and the same column.
- A value that sits on one printed sum only cannot be located when that sum fails; it is reported as "cannot verify".
  Three of the counties print only a row sum as the second check (`summary.md`, column "second sum").
- Limestone County prints nothing that can be added up, so it is listed as not checked and left as published.
- Where the scan's own printed totals disagree with each other, Crossfoot says so and lists it for a person. It does
  not say which is right.
- Some published rows were not compared with the scan (the contest did not pair with one on the scan, or the row
  repeats a precinct); each is listed in the run's `summary.md` under "Published rows compared with the scan".
- A missing or extra row is listed, never added or removed.
- A person still has to open the scan for each finding, confirm it, and send it to the project. None has been confirmed.
- Not built: sending anything to anyone, and reading a scan that has no printed totals.

## What existed before the event

The idea and the plan: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md), [UI-SPEC.md](UI-SPEC.md) and
[.prod-build/contract.md](.prod-build/contract.md) were written before any code. No code existed before the event.
`.prod-build/briefs/` and `.prod-build/reports/` hold the task given to each coding session and what it reported.

- A value that sits on one printed sum only cannot be located when that sum fails; it is reported as "cannot verify".

  not say which is right.
- Some published rows were not compared with the scan (the contest did not pair with one on the scan, or the row
  repeats a precinct); each is listed in the run's `summary.md` under "Published rows compared with the scan".

- A person still has to open the scan for each finding, confirm it, and send it to the project. None has been confirmed.

Crossfoot is an agent that audits published data against the scanned documents it was copied from, proves each
error with the document's own printed totals, and proposes the fix.

<!-- picture:start -->
<!-- picture:end -->

## What it found

Eight Texas county files for the 2024 general election, each checked against its county's own scan. Every figure
below is made from [`runs/20261011-141300/summary.json`](runs/20261011-141300/summary.json) by
[`tools/readme_tables.py`](tools/readme_tables.py); each county's own folder holds its report, corrected file and crops.

<!-- table:start -->
<!-- table:end -->

Confirmed by a person: 0. Nothing has been sent to the project.

What these are: transcription slips in a volunteer dataset, found by comparing it with the counties' certified scans,
which are the source of truth. The scans and the published files are public
([scans](https://github.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/tree/master/2024/general),
[published files](https://github.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/tree/master/2024/counties), from the
[OpenElections](https://github.com/openelections) project). Neither the project nor any county has seen or approved
this. Nothing here says anything about the results themselves.

How to check one: open the county's `report.md` (for example
[Panola's](runs/20261011-135350/panola/report.md)). Each group has a crop of the scan, the cells, and each printed sum
with the value that makes it hold. Add the numbers on the crop yourself.

## How it works

1. Read a sample of the first page with a cheap model and choose the reader by how many printed row sums fail.
2. Read every page into a ledger, one cell at a time.
3. Check every printed sum: a value is accepted only when the sums it sits on hold.
4. Where two failing sums cross, look again at that cell with a bigger crop and, if needed, a stronger model.
5. Lay the published file over the closed ledger, row by row.
6. The printed sums decide: a correction is proposed only when a printed total agrees with the new value and
   disagrees with the old one; otherwise it says "cannot verify" and leaves the value alone.
